# Naive Bayes – Iris Flower Classification

A Machine Learning project that uses the Gaussian Naive Bayes algorithm to classify Iris flowers into three different species.

## Overview

This project implements the Gaussian Naive Bayes algorithm using Scikit-learn. The goal is to predict the species of an Iris flower based on its sepal and petal measurements.

## Dataset

**Iris Dataset**

- **Source:** Scikit-learn built-in dataset
- **Total Samples:** 150
- **Features:** 4
- **Target:** Flower species
- **Classes:**
  - Setosa
  - Versicolor
  - Virginica

## Input Features

- Sepal Length
- Sepal Width
- Petal Length
- Petal Width

## Technologies

- Python
- Pandas
- Seaborn
- Matplotlib
- Scikit-learn

## Algorithm Implemented

1. Gaussian Naive Bayes

## Concepts Covered

- Dataset Loading
- Feature and Target Separation
- DataFrame Creation using Pandas
- Train-Test Split
- Gaussian Naive Bayes Model Training
- Model Prediction
- Accuracy Score
- Classification Report
- Confusion Matrix
- Data Visualization using Seaborn

## Implementation

- Loaded the Iris dataset using Scikit-learn.
- Separated input features and target labels.
- Split the dataset into training and testing sets (80:20).
- Trained a Gaussian Naive Bayes classifier.
- Predicted flower species using the test dataset.
- Evaluated the model using accuracy, classification report, and confusion matrix.

## Model Evaluation

The model is evaluated using:

- Accuracy Score
- Precision
- Recall
- F1-Score
- Confusion Matrix

## Goal

To understand how the Naive Bayes algorithm works and learn how to implement a probabilistic classification model using Scikit-learn.

## Note

This is an educational Machine Learning project using the Iris dataset.
